newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmakers reach accord on welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmakers reach accord on welfare reform.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson and legislative leaders on Monday reached a compromise on welfare reform that could help end the state's budget impasse, lawmakers said.

Wilson, a Republican, and Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, said the compromise plan would kick new welfare recipients off aid after 18 months and limit current recipients to 24 months of benefits.
Grant levels would be cut and counties would keep 100 percent of the savings. The plan would also provide a safety net for children on aid, the lawmakers said.
"This compromise preserves the safety net but moves people from welfare to work," Lockyer told reporters. "There's a major emphasis on protecting children and there's significant county flexibility."

Welfare reform has been the major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating the state's budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
The state Assembly and Senate could vote on the welfare reform plan on Thursday. Lawmakers said the welfare plan would make it easier to finalise the state budget.
